trust_decision.summary: Cache-key fidelity for PIL images is decided in the PIL branch of _CacheFuncHasher._to_bytes: two images must hash differently whenever their rendered content differs, so a P-mode image's colour palette has to enter the hash even though Image.tobytes() returns only palette indices.

landing_point.why: The advisory names 'PIL P-mode palette omission' in the @st.cache_data hasher; this is the only PIL branch in the caching hasher and the only place where Image.tobytes() is fed into the cache key.

fix_sites.entry_point: st.cache_data / st.cache_resource / st.cache decorated function calls, via CachedFunc._get_or_create_cached_value -> _make_value_key -> update_hash

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Large numpy/pandas/polars inputs are fingerprinted from a fixed 100k/10k-element sample by design (hashing.py:52-58; the same collision tradeoff is documented for media files at memory_media_file_storage.py:62-67), so a solver can argue sample-only collisions are accepted design and outside a report about PIL palettes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The value key must stay deterministic across processes/runs because a persist='disk' cache file is named after it (cache_utils.py:295-305 -> local_disk_cache_storage.py:208-212); a tempting over-broad fix that replaces the fixed sampling seed with a random or per-process seed stops caches surviving restarts.

O6_input_shapes: P-mode image with an explicit palette set via putpalette(): palette bytes are prepended to the pixel bytes before hashing
P-mode image whose getpalette() returns None: pixels only, unchanged
non-P-mode images (RGB, RGBA, L, ...): unchanged tobytes() path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: np.ndarray arguments with >= 500,000 elements are reduced to 100,000 elements chosen by np.random.RandomState(0); the PIL branch reuses this through to_bytes(np_array), so two large P-mode images whose palettes differ only at palette entries outside the fixed sample (or two arrays differing only outside it) still produce the same cache key.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Sampling large inputs with a fixed seed is the documented performance tradeoff (hashing.py:52-58, 544-545); a solver can call it intentional and out of scope for a palette bug.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, immediately above the landing point (0 files, 0 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Large pandas Series/DataFrames (>= 50,000 rows) are sampled with random_state=0 (polars with seed=0), so rows outside the fixed sample never affect the cache key.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about PIL images; dataframe sampling is a separate, documented large-data fingerprint that the published fix does not mention.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 100 lines above the landing point (0 files, 0 packages)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second hasher arm for an image-like wrapper or PIL plugin subclass that also projects pixels with tobytes()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the branch is a type-dispatch arm keyed on an exact FQN, so a maintainer adding support for another image type would copy it, palette omission included.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another large-value fingerprint (e.g. stride sampling np_obj[::n]) beside the RandomState(0) choice
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the module already carries three fixed-seed sampling schemes (numpy, pandas, polars) plus a head/middle/tail fingerprint in memory_media_file_storage.py:86-94, so a further variant is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-call-site key builder that hashes arguments itself instead of delegating to update_hash
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _make_value_key is already the composition point that produces the cache key, so an image 'fast path' would naturally be written there.
